messages:
Sam B.: Heads up — I'm drafting a customer-facing playbook + sample-checklist for the upcoming audit-event schema changes and the expanded coverage (RBAC decision events, KMS key use, sensitive-ops). Need a doc owner and a verification plan for customer validation. cc @Marta V. @Kevin L. :eyes:
Marta V.: I can take doc owner. Question: do we have canonical field names for the new RBAC events? want to avoid churn in 1.0 vs 1.1 schemas.
Kevin L.: We sketched a mapping earlier, here's a minimal example payload that should be in examples section: ```json
{
  "event_type": "rbac.change",
  "actor": {"id": "u_123", "email": "sam@example.com"},
  "resource": {"type": "model", "id": "m-xyz"},
  "action": "grant_role",
  "role": "inference_admin",
  "timestamp": "2024-05-01T15:23:12Z",
  "metadata": {"grant_method": "console", "request_id": "req-456"}
}
```
Alice R.: Nice. Add a short compatibility note: if customers map by `action` only, they should also consider `metadata.grant_method` for audit completeness.
Sam B.: Good call. Also we need to document KMS integration events (key.rotate, key.access). Example minimal: `event_type: kms.key_access`, `actor`, `key_id`, `operation`, `success` boolean, and `kms_context` for token provenance.
Marta V.: For the playbook, propose sections: 1) Summary & impact, 2) Field mapping & compatibility table, 3) Sample payloads, 4) Validation checklist for customers, 5) Migration steps + fallback behavior, 6) Changelog notes for admin console and API.
Kevin L.: For validation harness: I can produce a small `audit-validator` script (python) that checks required fields and flags name collisions. We'll ship a Postman collection + small Node validator too.
Sam B.: Action items: Marta = primary doc owner and release notes; Kevin = sample payloads + validator; Alice = customer messaging draft + support FAQ; DevEx = add examples to quickstart and SDK snippets. ETA: draft by 2024-05-07 for internal review.
DevEx: I'll schedule a short doc review slot on 2024-05-06 10:00 PT. Will add a checklist template in the doc so customers can run through it.
SecBot: Reminder — include regression tests that assert all audit-event names are covered in telemetry; link: https://go/reports/audit-coverage (internal).
Alice R.: For customer-facing changelog bullets (short): - Added RBAC change events (grant/revoke/role-update) - Added KMS key lifecycle events (create/rotate/delete/access) - Expanded audit schema with metadata for request provenance - Validation tools and sample payloads available
Sam B.: We should also include a short FAQ line for 'Will old logs break?': answer = we keep backward compatible `event_type` aliases for 90 days and publish mapping.
Kevin L.: Security note: KMS key_access events must avoid leaking plaintext key material — include key_id and operation only, never key bytes. Add that to docs and unit tests.
Marta V.: Draft uploaded to the draft-docs PR, link: https://git.internal/r/redwood/docs/pulls/1423. Please review and add comments before EOD Tuesday.
DeployBot: docs.redwood-internal deployment triggered for branch doc/audit-playbook (status: pending).
Sam B.: Thanks all — once internal signoff, we'll prepare the customer announcement cadence: 2-week preview, docs + sample pack, 1-week reminder, GA announcement.
Alice R.: I'll draft the customer email + changelog entry and post here tomorrow for review. :+1:
Kevin L.: I'll open a tiny repo with the validator and sample events and attach to the PR.
Sam B.: Closing note: keep the playbook concise — customers want checklist-style steps, not long essays. We'll keep the heavy detail in appendices and sample pack. :white_check_mark:
